claims.statement: The manufacturer's troubleshooting for espresso that runs out too quickly lists a too-coarse grind, too little coffee and too light a tamp, not the burrs.
The manufacturer says to use beans 5–20 days after the roasted-on date; stale coffee may pour too quickly and taste bitter and watery.
Use single-wall baskets with fresh beans; dual-wall baskets are for pre-ground coffee.
As a dose guide, the tamper's metal cap should sit level with the basket rim after tamping.
The booklet's burr cleaning (run empty, remove the top burr, brush burrs and chute) removes oil build-up that can impede performance.
The adjustable upper burr is a documented owner feature on both machines for a wider grind range; move it one number at a time and check the extraction after each adjustment.

A parts seller lists upper burr SP0027464 for machines with a PDC batch date of 1926 or later and SP0001801 for earlier machines; both listings name the Express and Pro, and the batch date is on the sticker under the machine.
The Smart Grinder Pro comes with a portafilter cradle for 50–54 mm portafilters.

CoffeeGeek's 2023 review says the Smart Grinder Pro uses a 40 mm conical burr group, the same one that was in the Barista Express; Seattle Coffee Gear's 2016 comparison found the Express burrs were conical stainless steel like the Smart Grinder Pro's.
CoffeeGeek's reviewer calls the Smart Grinder Pro a clumpy grinder for espresso that retains a lot of grounds.
An owner on OzBargain said the Smart Grinder Pro would not be an upgrade from the Barista Express built-in grinder; others suggested a DF54.
The Barista Pro's built-in grinder uses Baratza European Precision Burrs; no source compares them with the Smart Grinder Pro's burrs.
The DF54 is a single-dose grinder with 54 mm stainless flat burrs and stepless adjustment.
In Coffeeblog's review, DF54 retention was 0.1 g or less from the third use.
The single-dose workflow is to weigh each dose and transfer grounds from the dosing cup.
A reader says the DF54 cradle is made for 58 mm portafilters and a 54 mm portafilter can be pushed in and held.
Coffeeblog advises UK buyers to buy the DF54 from a UK retailer, warning that overseas sellers may ship an EU plug with no UK warranty and that import fees may apply.
The Encore ESP has 40 mm conical steel (M2) burrs with a quick-release burr mount.
Baratza identifies settings 1–20 as the Encore ESP's espresso range.
Baratza lists an Encore ESP dosing cup intended for 54 mm portafilters.
The Barista Express comes with a 54 mm portafilter, and the manufacturer lists a 54 mm portafilter for the Barista Pro.
